'''Ents''' are giant humanoids in [[J. R. R. Tolkien]]'s [[fantasy]] world of [[Middle-earth]] who closely resemble [[tree]]s; their leader is [[Treebeard]] of Fangorn forest. Their name is derived from an [[Old English]] word for "[[giant]]".

The Ents appear in ''[[The Lord of the Rings]]'' as ancient shepherds of the forest and allies of the free peoples of Middle-earth during the [[War of the Ring]]. The Ent who figures most prominently in the book is [[Treebeard]], who is called the oldest creature in Middle-earth. At that time, there are no young Ents (Entings) because the Entwives (female Ents) were lost. Akin to Ents are '''Huorns''', whom Treebeard describes as a transitional form of trees which become animated or, conversely, as Ents who grow more "treelike" over time.

Tolkien stated that he was disappointed by [[Shakespeare]]'s handling of the coming of "Great Birnam Wood to High Dunsinane hill"; he wanted a setting in which the trees would actually go to war. Commentators have seen this as wish-fulfilment, as he disliked the damage being done to the English countryside in his lifetime. Scholars have seen his tale of the Ents as a myth, mostly without analysing it. [[Corey Olsen]] interprets the song of the Ents and the Entwives as a myth that warns of the dangers of apathetically isolating oneself in nature, whereas the Ents' song "In the willow-meads of Tasarinan" is a lament.

Inspired by Tolkien and similar traditions, animated or [[anthropomorphic]] tree creatures appear in a variety of media and works of fantasy.

== Internal history ==

[[Treebeard]], called by [[Gandalf]] the oldest living Ent and the oldest living thing that walks in [[Middle-earth]],<ref name="The White Rider" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954}}, book 3, ch. 5: "The White Rider".</ref> is described as being around {{convert|14|ft|m|0}} tall, "Man-like, almost [[Troll (Middle-earth)|Troll]]-like", and clad in something that might have been tree-bark, with seven toes, a bushy, "almost twiggy" beard and deep penetrating eyes.<ref name="Treebeard" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954}}, book 3, ch. 4: "Treebeard".</ref> Ents vary widely in personal traits (height, heft, colouring, even the number of toes), having come to resemble somewhat the specific types of trees that they shepherded. [[Bregalad|Quickbeam]], for example, guarded [[Sorbus aucuparia|rowan]] trees and bore some resemblance to rowans: tall and slender, smooth-skinned, with ruddy lips and grey-green hair. Some Ents, such as Treebeard, were like<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>

{{blockquote|[[European beech|beech]]-trees or [[English oak|oaks]]. But there were other kinds. Some recalled the [[Castanea sativa|chestnut]]: brown-skinned Ents with large splayfingered hands, and short thick legs. Some recalled the [[Common ash|ash]]: tall straight grey Ents with many-fingered hands and long legs; some the [[Abies abies|fir]] (the tallest Ents), and others the [[Silver birch|birch]], ... and the [[Common linden|linden]].<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>}}

[[File:Twisted Plumeria tree trunk overgrowing the steep stone stairs of Wat Phou temple, Champasak, Laos.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|Like the roots of trees, but far more rapidly, Tolkien's Ents could break stone.<ref name="Flotsam and Jetsam" group=T/>]]

Ents are somewhat treelike, with extraordinarily tough skin; they can erode stone rapidly, but are vulnerable to fire and axe-strokes. They are patient and cautious, with a long sense of time; they considered a three-day deliberation "hasty".<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>

Ents are tall and very strong, capable of tearing apart rock and stone when "roused". Tolkien describes them as tossing great slabs of stone about, and ripping down the walls of Isengard "like bread-crust".<ref name="Flotsam and Jetsam" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954}}, book 3, ch. 9: "Flotsam and Jetsam".</ref> [[Treebeard]] boasted of their strength to [[Meriadoc Brandybuck|Merry]] and [[Peregrin Took|Pippin]]; he said that Ents were much more powerful than [[Troll (Middle-earth)|Trolls]], which [[Morgoth]] made in the [[First Age]] in mockery of Ents, as [[Orc]]s were of [[Elf (Middle-earth)|Elves]].<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>

=== First Age ===

Tolkien wrote almost nothing of the early history of the Ents. After the [[Dwarf (Middle-earth)|Dwarves]] were put to sleep by [[Eru Ilúvatar|Eru]] to await the coming of the Elves, the Vala [[Aulë]] told his wife [[Yavanna]], "the lover of all things that grow in the earth,"<ref group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1977}}, [[Valaquenta]]</ref> of the Dwarves. She replied, "They will delve in the earth, and the things that grow and live upon the earth they will not heed. Many a tree shall feel the bite of their iron without pity."<ref name="Of Aulë and Yavanna" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1977}}, "Quenta Silmarillion" ch. 2: "Of Aulë and Yavanna"</ref> She went to [[Manwë (Middle-earth)|Manwë]] and appealed to him to protect the trees, and they realized that Ents, too, were part of the [[Ainulindalë|Song of Creation]]. Yavanna then warned Aulë, "Now let thy children beware! For there shall walk a power in the forests whose wrath they will arouse at their peril." The Ents are called "the Shepherds of the Trees".<ref name="Of Aulë and Yavanna" group=T/> Much later, when [[Beren]] and a force of [[Green Elves]] waylay the force of [[Dwarf (Middle-earth)|Dwarves]] returning from the sack of [[Doriath (Middle-earth)|Doriath]], the Dwarves are routed and scatter into the wood, where the Shepherds of the Trees ensure that none escape.<ref group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1977}}, "Quenta Silmarillion", ch. 22 "Of the Ruin of Doriath"</ref>
Ents did not know how to speak until the Elves taught them. Treebeard said that the Elves "cured us of dumbness", calling that a great gift that could not be forgotten.<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/> At that time, much of [[Eriador]] was forested; [[Elrond]] stated that "a squirrel could go from tree to tree from what is now the Shire to [[Dunland]] west of Isengard."<ref name="Council of Elrond" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954a}}, book 2, ch. 2: "[[The Council of Elrond]]".</ref><ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>

=== Entwives ===

The Entwives began to move farther away from the Ents because they liked to plant and control things, while the Ents preferred forests and liked to let things take their natural course. The Entwives moved away to what became the Brown Lands across the Great River [[Geography of Middle-earth#Rhovanion|Anduin]], although the male Ents still visited them. The Entwives interacted with [[Men (Middle-earth)|Men]] and taught them the art of agriculture. The gardens of the Entwives  were destroyed by [[Sauron]], and the Entwives disappeared. It was sung by the Elves that one day the Ents and Entwives would find each other. Treebeard indeed implored the Hobbits to send word to him if they had news of the Entwives.<ref name="Many Partings" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1955}}, book 6, ch. 6 "Many Partings"</ref>

Tolkien spent much time considering the fate of the Entwives, stating in ''Letters'' #144: "I think that in fact the Entwives have disappeared for good, being destroyed with their gardens in the War of the Last Alliance...some may have fled east, or even have become enslaved..."<ref name="Letters 144" group=T>{{harvnb|Carpenter|2023|loc=#144 to [[Naomi Mitchison]], 25 April 1954 }}</ref>

After [[Aragorn]] is crowned king, he promised Treebeard that the Ents could prosper again and spread to new lands with the threat of [[Mordor]] gone, and renew their search for the Entwives. Treebeard lamented that forests may spread but the Ents would not, and he predicted that the few remaining Ents would remain in Fangorn forest and dwindle or become "treeish".<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/>

=== The Last March of the Ents ===

The Ents, angry at [[Saruman]] for cutting down their trees, convene an Entmoot.<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/> They decide to march on Saruman's fortress at [[Isengard]] - 'the last march of the Ents'. Led by Treebeard and accompanied by the [[hobbit]]s [[Meriadoc Brandybuck]] and [[Peregrin Took]], the Ents numbered about 50, plus an army of Huorns.<ref name="Treebeard" group=T/> They destroy Isengard, tearing down the wall around it:<ref name="Flotsam and Jetsam" group=T/> "If the [[Belegaer|Great Sea]] had risen in wrath and fallen on the hills with storm, it could have worked no greater ruin".<ref name="Road to Isengard" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954}}, book 3, ch. 8: "The Road to Isengard"</ref> Saruman is trapped in the tower of [[Orthanc]].<ref name="Flotsam and Jetsam" group=T/>

== Analysis ==

=== Etymology ===

{{see also|Isengard#Etymology}}

[[File:Orthanc enta geweorc in Maxims II manuscript.jpg|thumb|upright=2|The phrase ''orðanc enta geƿeorc'' (orthanc enta geweorc), on the second line of the Old English [[Maxims II]] manuscript, seems to have inspired Tolkien.<ref name="Shippey 2001 p88"/>]]

The word "Ent" is from the [[Old English]] ''[[wikt:ent#Old English|ent]]'' or ''[[wikt:eoten#Old English|eoten]]'', meaning "giant". Tolkien borrowed the word from a phrase in the Anglo-Saxon poems ''[[The Ruin]]'' and ''[[Maxims II]]'', ''orðanc enta geƿeorc'' (orthanc enta geweorc, "cunning work of giants"),<ref name="Shippey 2001 p88">{{cite book |first=Tom |last=Shippey |author-link=Tom Shippey |title=J. R. R. Tolkien – Author of the Century |publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|Houghton Mifflin]] |year=2001 |page=88 |isbn=978-0-618-12764-1}}</ref> which describes [[Ancient Rome|Roman]] ruins.<ref group=T>{{harvnb|Carpenter|2023|loc=#163 to [[W. H. Auden]], 7 June 1955 }}</ref>{{sfn|Shippey|2005|p=149}}

In [[Sindarin]], one of Tolkien's invented [[Elvish language]]s, the word for Ent is ''Onod'' (plural ''Enyd''). The Sindarin word ''Onodrim'' means the Ents as a race.<ref group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1980}} Index, entries for ''Ent'', ''Enyd'', and ''Onodrim''.</ref>

=== Improving on Shakespeare ===

{{further|Shakespeare's influence on Tolkien}}

{{multiple image
 |direction   = horizontal
 |total_width = 500
 |image1      = An old, damaged oak, Savernake Forest - geograph.org.uk - 344479.jpg
 |caption1    = Tolkien wrote that he "longed to devise a setting in which the trees might really march to war", unlike the "shabby" treatment of the story in [[William Shakespeare|Shakespeare]]'s ''[[Macbeth]]''.<ref name="Birnam Wood letter" group=T/>
 |image2      = Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane. Illustration for Macbeth, 1912.jpg
 |caption2    = Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane, in the form of branches carried by the soldiers, as described by Shakespeare.
}}

Tolkien noted in a letter that he had created Ents in response to his "bitter disappointment and disgust from schooldays with the shabby use made in [[William Shakespeare|Shakespeare]]'s ''[[Macbeth]]'' of the coming of 'Great [[Birnam Wood]] to high Dunsinane hill': I longed to devise a setting in which the trees might really march to war".<ref name="Birnam Wood letter" group=T>{{harvnb|Carpenter|2023|loc=No. 163, footnote, pp. 211–212. }}</ref> The Ents ensured victory at the [[Battle of Helm's Deep]] by herding a forest of angry, tree-like Huorns there, to destroy Saruman's army of [[Orc]]s.<ref name="Helm's Deep" group=T>{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954}}, book 3, ch. 7 "Helm's Deep"</ref>

=== Other sources ===

[[Nick Groom]] suggests some other possible sources, besides Shakespeare. The [[Gospel of Mark]] has the speech by a man cured of blindness "I see men as trees, walking."(Mark 8:24) [[Algernon Blackwood]]'s 1912 story "The Man Whom the Trees Loved" suggests that "trees had once been moving things, animal organisms of some sort, that had stood so long feeding, sleeping, dreaming, or something, in the same place, that they had lost the power to get away", which Groom remarks sounds just like Treebeard's account of Ents going "sleepy and 'tree-ish'".{{sfn|Groom|2022|p=148}} He notes, too, [[Arthur Rackham]]'s drawings with "bristly, twisted, anthropomorphic trees that appear as the guises of Elves and other supernatural beings", while [[Disney]]'s 1932 ''[[Silly Symphony]]'' episode ''[[Flowers and Trees]]'' features trees that walk.{{sfn|Groom|2022|p=148}}

Edward Pettit, writing in ''[[Mallorn (journal)|Mallorn]]'', notes that the Tolkien scholar [[Verlyn Flieger]] linked Treebeard to the Green Knight in the medieval romance ''[[Sir Gawain and the Green Knight]]''. Both figures have, Pettit writes, been suspected of being versions of the medieval [[Green Man]], the leafy figure often depicted in sculptures in churches. Old English in addition has trees that speak in the alliterative poem ''[[The Dream of the Rood]]''.<ref name="Pettit 2004">{{cite journal |last=Pettit |first=Edward |title=Treebeard's roots in medieval European tradition |journal=[[Mallorn (journal)|Mallorn]] |date=2004 |issue=42 |pages=11-18 |url=https://journals.tolkiensociety.org/mallorn/article/download/125/119/237}}</ref>

<gallery class=center mode=nolines widths=180 heights=180>
File:04 -Wils and shy and monstrous creatures ranged in her plains and forests-.jpg|[[Arthur Rackham]]'s drawings feature twisted trees that suggest supernatural beings.{{sfn|Groom|2022|p=148}}
File:Ludlow Green Man misericord.jpg|The Ent Treebeard has been thought to be a version of the [[Green Man]],<ref name="Pettit 2004"/> seen here on a medieval [[misericord]] in [[Ludlow, Shropshire|Ludlow]].
</gallery>

=== Wish-fulfilment and environmentalism ===

{{further|Environmentalism in The Lord of the Rings}}

Commentators have observed that having the Ents march to war against the tree-destroyers represented a wish-fulfilment on Tolkien's part, concerned as he was with the increasing damage to the English countryside in the 20th century.{{sfn|Shippey|2005|p=184}}<ref name="Niiler 1999">{{cite journal |last=Niiler |first=Lucas P. |title=Green Reading: Tolkien, Leopold and the Land Ethic |journal=[[Journal of the Fantastic in the Arts]] |date=1999 |volume=10 |issue=3 (39) |pages=276–285 |jstor=43308393}}</ref> In their book ''Ents, Elves, and Eriador: The Environmental Vision of J.R.R. Tolkien'', [[Matthew T. Dickerson]] and [[Jonathan Evans (scholar)|Jonathan Evans]] see Treebeard as vocalizing a vital part of [[Environmentalism in The Lord of the Rings|Tolkien's environmental ethic]], the need to preserve and look after every kind of wild place, especially forests.{{sfn|Dickerson|Evans|2006|pp=119–144, 250}}
[[Corey Olsen]] however criticises Dickerson and Evans's use of the Ents as "mere symbols".<ref name="Olsen 2008">{{cite journal |last=Olsen |first=Corey |author-link=Corey Olsen |title=The Myth of the Ent and the Entwife |journal=[[Tolkien Studies]] |publisher=[[Project Muse]] |volume=5 |issue=1 |year=2008 |issn=1547-3163 |doi=10.1353/tks.0.0013 |pages=39–53}}</ref>

=== Mythic value: song of the Ents and the Entwives===

[[C. S. Lewis]] described Tolkien's tale of the Ents as a myth, "a story which has a value in itself".<ref>{{cite book |last=Lewis |first=C. S. |author-link=C. S. Lewis |chapter=The Dethronement of Power |title=[[Understanding The Lord of the Rings]] |editor1=Rose A. Zimbardo |editor2=Neil D. Isaacs |location=Boston |publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|Houghton Mifflin]] |year=2004 |pages=11–15}}</ref> Ruth Noel likened the Ents to [[Germanic paganism|Germanic legends]] of "huge, wild, hairy [[Wild man|woodsprites]]".<ref>{{cite book |last=Noel |first=Ruth S. |title=The Mythology of Middle-earth |location=Boston |publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|Houghton Mifflin]]  |year=1977 |page=130}}</ref>

{{Quote box
 | title  = From the "Song of the Ents and Entwives"
 | quote  = <poem>Ent:

When Summer lies upon the world, and in a noon of gold
Beneath the roof of sleeping leaves the dreams of trees unfold,
When woodland halls are green and cool, and wind is in the West,
Come back to me! Come back to me, and say my land is best!

Entwife:

When Summer warms the hanging fruit and burns the berry brown;
When straw is gold, and ear is white, and harvest comes to town;
When honey spills, and apple swells, though wind be in the West,
I'll linger here beneath the Sun, because my land is best!</poem>
 | source = 
 | width  = 35em
 | align  = right
}}

Olsen sees in Tolkien's song of the Ents and the Entwives, supposedly written by Elves, "compelling insights on the complexities and conflicts of life in a fallen world."<ref name="Olsen 2008"/> The song goes through the four seasons of the year, each time with a stanza by the Ent and then one by the Entwife. Olsen comments that the Ent is passive, even "languid and somnolent" in summer, the only active process being dreaming; whereas the Entwife's summer season is "simply bursting with activity". These are perhaps, Olsen reflects, not in competition; both contemplation and action are "valuable ways of celebrating natural beauty".<ref name="Olsen 2008"/> He suggests that Treebeard's view of the song is however biased, and that the Ent is not as humble as he claims to be, especially with respect to the Entwives. If the Ents and the Entwives were to be "unified", they would "balance and complete each other", but they face "moral dangers" without such balance: in the case of the Ents, the danger is of letting their life in nature "lapse into mere lassitude". He gives as examples the "apathetic isolationism" of Skinbark, who refuses to come out of his hills, and Leaflock's "somnolent oblivion", just standing in the long grass all summer doing nothing. Olsen calls it "a cautionary tale" and "tragic", quite unlike Treebeard's "In the willow-meads of Tasarinan", again covering the four seasons, but which is a lament.<ref name="Olsen 2008"/>

Anne Petty comments that the song follows traditional gender stereotypes, the Ents liking wild nature, the Entwives preferring the more domestic realm of tamed nature and gardening.<ref>{{cite book |last=Petty |first=Anne |title=Tolkien in the Land of Heroes: Discovering the Human Spirit |location=Cold Spring Harbor, New York |publisher=Cold Spring Press |year=2003 |page=242}}</ref>

== Adaptations ==

=== In other media ===

In [[Peter Jackson]]'s films ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers]]'' (2002) and ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King]]'' (2003), Treebeard is a combination of a large [[Audio-Animatronics|animatronic model]] and a [[computer generated imagery|CGI]] construct; he is voiced by [[John Rhys-Davies]], who also portrays [[Gimli (Middle-earth)|Gimli]].<ref name="Empire 2012">{{cite web |last=Nathan |first=Ian |title=The Making Of The Two Towers |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/two-towers/ |publisher=[[Empire Cinemas]] |access-date=28 March 2020 |date=23 October 2012 |orig-year=2002 <!--issue 163--> |quote=Treebeard will mainly be a CGI creation; this animatronic version is used for the close-ups with Hobbit actors Billy Boyd and Dominic Monaghan.}}</ref> [[The Fall of Troy (band)|The Fall of Troy]] has a song entitled "The Last March of the Ents" on their self-titled debut album released in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/the-fall-of-troy-mw0000322295|title=The Fall of Troy at AllMusic|website=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref> Permission was granted for a [[statue]] of [[Treebeard]] by [[Tim Tolkien]], near his great-uncle J. R. R. Tolkien's former home in [[Moseley]], [[Birmingham]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.moseleystatue.org/ |title=Moseley Statue |date=5 September 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051103152711/http://moseleystatue.org/ |archive-date=3 November 2005 |access-date=25 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tolkien statue gets the go ahead |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/west_midlands/6412017.stm |website=[[BBC News]] |date=2 March 2007 |quote=The statue was approved by Birmingham City Council planners at a meeting on Thursday [1 March 2007] night. }}</ref>

The TV series ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power]]'', set in the [[Second Age]], features Ents.<ref>{{cite web |last=Skrebels |first=Joe |title=Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power - New Teaser Shows Off Ents and More |date=6 July 2022 |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-new-teaser-shows-off-ents-and-more |publisher=[[IGN]] |access-date=7 October 2022}}</ref> Two of the Ents that appear in the [[The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 2|season two]] episode "[[Eldest (The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power)|Eldest]]" are Snaggleroot and Winterbloom (voiced by [[Jim Broadbent]] and [[Olivia Williams]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bardini |first=Julio |date=September 7, 2024 |title=Who Are the Ents in 'The Rings of Power' Season 2? |url=https://collider.com/rings-of-power-season-2-ents-explained/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907150132/https://collider.com/rings-of-power-season-2-ents-explained/ |archive-date=September 7, 2024 |access-date=September 7, 2024 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]}}</ref>).

=== In popular culture ===

[[File:Treant.png|thumb|upright=0.6|A "treant" from ''[[World of Warcraft]]'']]
Ents appeared in the earliest edition of the roleplaying game ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]'' in the [[Dungeons & Dragons (1974)|1974 white box set]], where they were described as tree-like creatures able to command trees, and lawful in nature.<ref>[[Gary Gygax|Gygax, Gary]], and [[Dave Arneson]]. ''Dungeons & Dragons'' (3-Volume Set) (TSR, 1974)</ref> In 1975, Elan Merchandising, which owned the game licence to the Tolkien estate, issued a cease-and-desist order regarding the use of the word "ent", so the ''Dungeons & Dragons'' creatures were renamed "treants".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Witwer |first1=Michael |last2=Newman |first2=Kyle |last3=Witwer |first3= Sam |title=Dungeons & Dragons Art & Arcana: A Visual History |publisher=[[Ten Speed Press]] |date=2018|isbn=978-0399580949 |page=71}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Gygax |first=Gary |author-link=Gary Gygax |title=Gary Gygax (Interview) |website=TheOneRing.net |url=http://archives.theonering.net/features/interviews/gary_gygax.html#maincontent |access-date=7 October 2008}}</ref> ''[[Heroes of Might and Magic V]]'' includes Treants as a part of the Elven alliance; however, due to copyright infringement issues, their look was changed<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heroesofmightandmagic.com/heroes5/mods_and_fixes.shtml |title=Mods and fixes |website=Heroes of Might and Magic |access-date=2 October 2020}}</ref> between the beta phase and the retail version, making them [[quadrupedal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heroesofmightandmagic.com/heroes5/sylvan_creatures.shtml#CREATURE_TREANT |title=Sylvan creatures |website=Heroes of Might and Magic |access-date=2 October 2020}}</ref>
